title: The TRUSTED_NETWORK operand in ZPA policy rules

prose.text: This subject covers the TRUSTED_NETWORK policy operand.

prose.label: What the provider checks.
prose.text: {{validator-by-generation}} {{v1-lookup}} {{v2-no-lookup}} The two validators disagree on `rhs` {{divergence:rhs-false-accepted}}. What a false condition means is open {{gap:rhs-false-semantics}}. What a wrong identifier does is open {{gap:wrong-id-effect}}.
How the provider writes these rules and what it loses: [[zpa.terraform.policy-rule-writes]]. The identifiers: [[zpa.trusted-networks.object]].

checks.do: Whether the operand's lhs is the trusted network's networkId and not its id.
Which rule resource generation is in use, which decides which rhs values pass validation.
Whether a false condition is being relied on to target off-network users, which no source settles.
Whether the rule's client type is Client Connector, since the criterion works only there.

console-criterion.statement: In an access policy rule, Client Connector Trusted Networks is a criterion naming the type of network the user is connected to that Zscaler Client Connector can trust. Selecting several trusted networks combines them with OR.

quotes: Client Connector Trusted Networks: The type of network the user is connected to that Zscaler Client Connector can trust.
If you added multiple trusted networks to the policy rule, Private Access uses an OR Boolean operator between them.

client-connector-only.statement: Rules that use the Web Browser or Internet & SaaS Service Edge client types cannot also use posture profile or trusted network criteria; those criteria work only with Client Connector.

quotes: Rules using the Web Browser or Internet & SaaS Service Edge client types can not also use posture profiles or trusted networks criteria. The posture profiles or trusted networks criteria only work with Client Connector.

operand-v1.statement: In the v1 access, forwarding, inspection and isolation rule resources (`zpa_policy_access_rule`, `zpa_policy_forwarding_rule`, `zpa_policy_inspection_rule`, `zpa_policy_isolation_rule`), a trusted network condition is an operand with `object_type = "TRUSTED_NETWORK"`, `lhs` set to the trusted network's `network_id` and `rhs = "true"`.

operand-v2.statement: In v2 policy rule resources the trusted network operand has `entry_values` whose `lhs` is the trusted network's `network_id` and whose `rhs` is documented as `"true"` or `"false"`.

evidence.after: `object_type` (String) This is for specifying the policy criteria. Supported values: `TRUSTED_NETWORK`

rule-resources.statement: The provider documents `TRUSTED_NETWORK` as an operand for the access, forwarding, inspection and isolation policy rules in their v1 and v2 forms, and for the browser protection rule.

v1-lookup.statement: For v1 policy rule resources the provider looks the `lhs` up by `networkId` through the SDK's GetByNetID, so a value that is not a known `networkId` fails validation, and it requires `rhs` to be exactly `"true"`.

rhs-false-accepted.summary: Whether `rhs = "false"` is a legal trusted network condition depends on the rule resource generation: the v1 validator accepts only "true", the v2 validator and the v2 document accept "false".

positions.says: The v1 validator rejects any `rhs` other than "true".

quotes: rhs value must be 'true' or 'false' for TRUSTED_NETWORK object_type

evidence.after: `object_type` (String) This is for specifying the policy criteria. Supported values: `TRUSTED_NETWORK`

positions.says: The v2 document lists `"true"` or `"false"` for `rhs`, while its own value table lists `"true"`.

rhs-false-accepted.impact: The same condition passes plan in a v2 rule and fails in a v1 rule. Neither validator says what the server does with "false".

rhs-false-semantics.title: What ZPA does with a TRUSTED_NETWORK condition whose rhs is false
rhs-false-semantics.detail: The v2 validator and document allow `rhs = "false"`, but no source states whether the server evaluates it as "the user is not on this trusted network". Build a rule with `rhs = "false"` and observe matching on and off the network.
rhs-false-semantics.blocks: using a false condition to target off-network users

wrong-id-effect.title: What a rule does when the lhs is the object id instead of the networkId
wrong-id-effect.detail: Unverified legacy statement: "If you set lhs to the object id instead of network_id, the condition silently never matches." The v1 provider validation rejects an `lhs` that is not a known `networkId`, and the v2 validation does not check it; no source says what the server does with a value that is not a `networkId`. Create a v2 rule with the object id and test matching from a device on the network.
wrong-id-effect.blocks: explaining a never-matching trusted network rule by the identifier
